source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Having heard that exceedingly wonderful speech of Lakshmana, Rama became very pleased and indeed spoke these words.
verses.2: Indeed, such a kinsman as you, O greatly intelligent and gentle one, who follows my mind, is rare to find, especially in these times.
verses.3: O one with auspicious marks, listen carefully to what is in my heart, and having heard it, carry out my command.
verses.4: O gentle Lakshmana, the neglect of the citizens' work for four days indeed pierces my vital parts.
verses.5: O best among men, let the principal officers, the chief priest, the ministers, and also the men and women seeking justice be summoned.
verses.6: There is no doubt that a king who does not attend to the affairs of his citizens daily falls into a terrible, enclosed hell.
verses.7: Indeed, it is heard that formerly there was a very famous king named Nṛga, a protector of the earth, who was devoted to Brahmins, truthful, and pure.
verses.8: That king, Nṛga, once at Pushkara, gave crores of cows, along with their calves and adorned with gold, to the Brahmins.
verses.9: O sinless one, then that cow with its calf, having come into contact, was taken by a poor Brahmana who maintained sacred fires and lived by gleaning.
verses.10: Afflicted by hunger, he searched for his lost cow here and there in all kingdoms for many years but could not find it.
verses.11: Then, having gone to Kanakhala, he saw his own cow, whose calf had grown old and was healthy, in the dwelling of the Brahmana.
verses.12: Then that Brahmana called her by her own name, saying, "Come, Shabala!" and the cow indeed heard his voice.
verses.13: Having recognized the voice of that hungry Brahmana, the cow indeed followed him from behind as he, radiant like fire, walked away.
verses.14: The brahmin who was tending the cow also quickly followed it, and having gone, swiftly told that sage, "This is my cow."
verses.15: One brahmin claimed the cow was touched by the king, while the other insisted it was given to him by Nṛga, leading to a great dispute between the two learned brahmins.
verses.16: Then, disputing with each other, they approached the giver (King Nṛga), but those two did not meet King Nṛga at the palace gate.
verses.17: After staying for many days and nights, those two great-souled and best among brahmins became exceedingly angry and spoke terrible words filled with a curse.
verses.18: Because you do not grant an audience to petitioners for the accomplishment of their purpose, you shall become a chameleon, invisible to all beings.
verses.19: For many thousands and hundreds of years, you will indeed reside in this pit as a chameleon for a long duration.
verses.20: Indeed, in this world, Vishnu, renowned as Vasudeva, the increaser of the Yadus' glory and having a human form, will be born.
verses.21: O King, he will be your liberator from that curse, and by him, your expiation will be accomplished in due course.
verses.22: Indeed, both Nara and Narayana, greatly powerful, will be born for the purpose of alleviating the earth's burden when the Kali Yuga has arrived.
verses.23: Thus, having pronounced the curse, those two Brahmins, now free from distress, indeed gave that weak, old cow to a Brahmin.
verses.24: In this manner, that king experiences that very terrible curse.
verses.25: Indeed, the crowding of petitioners leads to harm for kings; therefore, let the petitioners quickly approach me for an audience.
verses.26: Indeed, the fruit of a well-done work is not lost, O king; therefore, O son of Sumitra, go and wait for any person who has business. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 53 ।। Thus ends the fifty-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
